title: Pump: cavitation and dry running
text: Dry running or cavitation causes grinding or rattling noise, falling outlet pressure and rapid seal and bearing damage. Running dry beyond 2 minutes requires seal inspection. Check suction line, strainer and fluid level.

title: Pump: bearing failure symptoms
text: Worn bearings cause grinding noise, bearing temperature above 80 C and vibration above 7.1 mm/s. Inspect lubrication, shaft alignment and bearing play. Above 95 C stop the pump.

title: Pump: mechanical seal leakage
text: Seal leakage appears as dripping near the shaft, often after dry running or misalignment. Replace the seal if leakage exceeds 10 drops per minute.

title: Pump: motor overheating
text: Motor temperature above 90 C indicates overload, blocked ventilation, voltage imbalance or bearing drag. Check fan cover, supply voltage and current draw. Above 110 C stop the pump.

title: Pump: low outlet pressure or flow
text: Outlet pressure below 1.5 bar with normal motor current points to a blocked strainer, partly closed suction valve, air in the suction line or a worn impeller. Below 0.8 bar stop the pump. Check strainer, valve positions and priming.

title: Pump: impeller wear and damage
text: A worn or damaged impeller reduces pressure and flow and can cause vibration and a rattling sound. Look for eroded vane edges, debris lodged in the passages and rubbing against the casing. Replace the impeller if vanes are cracked or badly eroded.

title: Pump: vibration and misalignment
text: Vibration above 7.1 mm/s suggests shaft misalignment, loose baseplate bolts, unbalanced impeller or cavitation. Above 11 mm/s stop the pump. Check coupling alignment, foundation bolts and suction conditions.

title: Pump: abnormal noise guide
text: Grinding or growling noise usually comes from bearings. Crackling like gravel indicates cavitation. A high squeal can come from a dry or damaged seal. A rhythmic knock suggests a loose coupling or impeller contact.

title: Compressor: high discharge temperature
text: Discharge temperature above 110 C suggests low oil, fouled cooler or worn valves. Above 130 C shut down. Check oil level, cooler fins and intake filter.

title: Compressor: low oil pressure
text: Oil pressure below 1.5 bar risks bearing damage. Check oil level, oil filter and oil pump. Below 0.8 bar shut down immediately.

title: Compressor: abnormal vibration
text: Vibration above 7.1 mm/s can come from loose mountings, worn bearings, a damaged coupling or liquid carry-over. Above 11 mm/s shut down. Check mounting bolts, coupling condition and the separator drain.

title: Compressor: reduced output or slow pressure build-up
text: Slow pressure build-up points to worn or leaking valves, a clogged intake filter, leaking piping or worn piston rings. Inspect the intake filter first, then test the system for air leaks.

title: Compressor: frequent trips
text: Repeated trips on temperature or pressure can follow a blocked cooler, low oil, a faulty pressure switch or a blocked unloader. Review the trip log and confirm the sensor reading with a separate gauge before replacing parts.

title: Motor: winding overheating
text: Winding temperature above 120 C indicates overload, phase imbalance or poor cooling. Above 140 C stop the motor. Measure current on all phases and inspect cooling airflow.

title: Motor: abnormal vibration
text: Vibration above 4.5 mm/s suggests misalignment, loose mounting, unbalanced rotor or worn bearings. Above 7.1 mm/s stop the motor. Check coupling alignment and foundation bolts.

title: Motor: humming or failure to start
text: A motor that hums but does not turn may have lost one supply phase, a seized load or a failed capacitor or starter. Do not keep trying to start it. Check supply on all phases and try to turn the shaft by hand with power locked off.

title: Motor: overload trips
text: Repeated overload trips come from a mechanically overloaded machine, low supply voltage, phase loss or a wrongly set overload relay. Compare measured current with the nameplate value before changing relay settings.

title: Motor: moisture and insulation problems
text: After wet conditions or long idle periods, insulation resistance can fall. Measure insulation resistance with a megger before restarting. A low reading means the windings need drying or rewinding.

title: General: restart after power loss
text: After a power cut, check phase sequence, lubrication state and that suction and discharge valves are in the correct position before judging a fault.

title: General: priority guidance
text: Urgent: safety risk or critical threshold exceeded. High: warning thresholds exceeded with active symptoms. Medium: intermittent symptoms. Low: cosmetic or monitoring only.

title: General: conflicting or missing sensor data
text: When two sensors disagree by more than 10 percent, or a reading is missing, confirm the value with a portable instrument before acting. Treat the worse reading as the working value until verified.

title: General: safety before inspection
text: Isolate and lock out power before opening guards or touching rotating parts. Allow hot surfaces to cool. Only a trained technician should open pressurised equipment.

title: General: recording findings
text: After inspection, record what was observed, what was measured and what was confirmed as the cause. Keep suspected causes separate from confirmed findings so later fault history stays reliable.
